chief_complaint: burning gritty eyes worsening at end of day, dry room
hpi_details: A 26-year-old woman presents with several weeks of bilateral burning and gritty eyes, worse late in the day and in dry rooms. She denies eye pain, photophobia, purulent discharge, and reduced vision.
ideas: She thinks staring at a computer screen all day under the office air conditioning is irritating and straining her eyes.
concerns: She is worried that her eyes will get so irritated that she will be unable to focus on her screen and fall behind at work.
expectations: She hopes to get soothing prescription eye drops that can quickly relieve the gritty feeling during her workday.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Dry eye syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Dry eye syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Dry Eye Syndrome: Preservative-free artificial tears QID, warm compresses, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: burning gritty eyes worsening at end of day, dry room

Key HPI features: A 26-year-old female presents to the clinic with burning gritty eyes worsening at end of day, dry room. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Dry Eye Syndrome.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Dry eye syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Blepharitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe unresponsive cases risk corneal complications.
management_principles: Plan for Dry Eye Syndrome: Preservative-free artificial tears QID, warm compresses
Assess the ocular surface and urgently refer for eye pain, photophobia, reduced vision, or persistent symptoms despite treatment
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

history.answer: My eyes have been burning and feeling gritty for several weeks, especially late in the day.
It started gradually about three or four weeks ago in both eyes, and it has been getting worse recently.
My eyes get a little pink all over by the evening, but I don't see any deep redness around the iris or distinct bloody spots.
It feels like there is sand or grit in both eyes with a burning sensation, but no deep throbbing ache or sharp pain.
It is definitely worse towards the end of the workday and in the evening, but better in the morning after I wake up.
My vision is normal, though sometimes my eyes get tired and slightly blurry after hours on the computer until I blink.
No, looking at light doesn't hurt my eyes.
No, I haven't seen any halos or rainbow rings around lights, and I have no headaches or nausea.
I don't have any yellow or green pus, and my eyelids aren't glued shut in the morning, just occasional watery tearing.
No, they don't really itch; they mostly burn and feel irritated.
No, my eyelids are not swollen, and there are no crusts or flakes along my eyelashes.
Moving my eyes doesn't hurt at all, my eyes don't bulge, and I have not had any fever.
No, I haven't had a cold or sore throat, and nobody at home or work has pink eye.
I don't wear contact lenses, only glasses when I work on the computer.
No, I haven't hit my eye, gotten chemicals in it, or had any foreign object fly into it.
No, I don't have seasonal allergies, hay fever, asthma, or eczema.
I work as an office clerk staring at computer screens for eight hours a day in an air-conditioned room, which makes it much worse.
I have felt a bit tired lately from work, but my mouth is not unusually dry and I produce normal saliva.
No, I have no morning back stiffness, joint pain or swelling, and no mouth sores.
No, I have never had shingles, cold sores, or blisters on my face or nose.
No, I don't take blood thinners, and I haven't had severe coughing, vomiting, or heavy lifting.
No, I have never had eye surgery, glaucoma, or serious eye infections before.
I bought some over-the-counter redness-relieving drops last week, but they only helped for a few minutes and then felt worse.
I thought maybe staring at my computer monitor all day under the blasting office air conditioner is just drying my eyes out and straining them.

I'm worried this constant burning will make it impossible to get through my workday without squinting and falling behind on my projects. I was hoping you could prescribe some strong lubricating drops to take away the gritty feeling so I can work comfortably.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or thyroid problems.
I have never had surgery or been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription medications or supplements, just those over-the-counter eye drops.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I drink socially, maybe one or two glasses of wine or beer on the weekend.
I work full-time in an office and live alone in an apartment.
Nobody in my family has autoimmune diseases, glaucoma, or serious eye conditions.
My last period started two weeks ago, and my cycles are regular every 28 days.
We use barrier protection consistently, and there is no chance that I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Alert, comfortable young woman sitting upright in no acute distress.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 70 beats/min, respiration 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.6 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Mild bilateral conjunctival hyperaemia without ciliary flush or subconjunctival hemorrhage, and sclerae are clear.
Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, pupils are round and equally reactive without defect, extraocular movements are intact without pain, and upper eyelid eversion reveals no foreign bodies.
No facial rashes, vesicular lesions over the forehead or tip of the nose, or flaking along the lid margins.
Oral mucosa is moist and pink with normal salivary pooling and no aphthous ulcers.
No peripheral joint tenderness, swelling, erythema, or limitation of range of motion.
